title: In-Band Single-Frequency Signaling; Signaling Systems for Control of Telephone Switching (Multifrequency Pulsing)
author: Weaver, A. & Newell, N. A., et al.
publication: Bell System Technical Journal, Vol. 39 No. 6 (Nov 1960), pp. 1319-1408
note: The primary source for R1 MF and 2600 Hz SF supervision. BSTJ 1960 defines one KP and one ST; the 700+1700 and 900+1700 combinations are 'Code 11' / 'Code 12' with no semantic names.

title: GR-506-CORE, LSSGR: Signaling for Analog Interfaces
author: Bellcore / Telcordia
note: Authoritative telco-side ACTS coin-signal timing: nickel 1x66ms, dime 2x66/66ms, quarter 5x33/33ms, dollar 1x650ms. p.249.

title: TR-NPL-000275, MF Signaling
author: Bellcore
note: Later Bell notation promoting the paired KP1/KP2 + ST/ST2P/ST3P scheme; MF tolerance +/-1.5%, level -7 dBm0/freq.

title: CCITT Blue Book (1988): Q.310-Q.332 (No.5), Q.400-Q.490 (R2), Q.140/Q.180 (No.6), Q.700 (No.7), Q.23/Q.24 (DTMF)
author: CCITT / ITU-T
note: International signaling. No.5 line signals use 2400 Hz and 2600 Hz; DTMF timing and twist per Q.24.

title: A REAL Functioning RED BOX Schematic
author: J.R. "Bob" Dobbs
note: Community-canon ACTS timing that homebrew red boxes actually emitted: nickel 60ms, dime 2x60/60ms, quarter 5x35/35ms. Widely repeated 1985-2005.

title: Converting a Tone Dialer into a Red Box
author: Noah Clayton
note: Original publication of the Radio Shack 43-141 crystal-swap (3.579545 MHz -> 6.5536 MHz) red-box procedure.

title: Secrets of the Little Blue Box
author: Ron Rosenbaum
note: Historical framing, not a technical primary source.

title: MIL-STD-187-100, Military Communications System Technical Standards (AUTOVON precedence)
author: US Department of Defense
note: Authoritative AUTOVON precedence mapping: A=Flash Override, B=Flash, C=Immediate, D=Priority. Some community sources reverse C and D.

title: ITU-T O-series (transmission measuring equipment)
author: ITU-T
note: Test-tone and level-measurement practice; the 1004/1020 Hz reference tone family.
